SL-000011.transcript:
Member (Owen Wilson): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Owen Wilson, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Wilson): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Wilson): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): When did you go off work?
Member (Owen Wilson): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Owen Wilson): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Owen Wilson): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Owen Wilson): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Owen Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Owen Wilson): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Owen Wilson): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Owen Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000011.narrative_summary: Owen Wilson, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a disability claim status case. Agent Sophie Belanger reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000018.transcript:
Member (Owen Singh): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Owen Singh, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Singh): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Singh): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Singh): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Owen Singh): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Owen Singh): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Owen Singh): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Owen Singh): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Owen Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Owen Singh): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Owen Singh): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Owen Singh): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Owen Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000058.transcript:
Member (Tyler Patel): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Tyler Patel, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Patel): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Patel): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Tyler Patel): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Tyler Patel): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Tyler Patel): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Tyler Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Tyler Patel): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Tyler Patel): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Tyler Patel): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Tyler Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.
SL-000058.narrative_summary: Tyler Patel, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a disability claim status case. Agent Daniel Okafor reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list. In the end, it was not resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000067.transcript:
Member (Noah Morrison): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Noah Morrison, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Morrison): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Morrison): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Noah Morrison): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Noah Morrison): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Noah Morrison): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Noah Morrison): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Noah Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Noah Morrison): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Noah Morrison): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Noah Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000067.narrative_summary: Noah Morrison, a Sun Life member, contacted support on an additional information request case. Member (Liam Morrison): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Liam Morrison, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Liam Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam Morrison): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.

Member (Liam Morrison): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Liam Morrison): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Liam Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Hannah Kim): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Hannah Kim): Who follows up?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Hannah Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Ahmed): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.

Member (Fatima Roy): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Fatima Roy, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Roy): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Fatima Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Fatima Roy): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Fatima Roy): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Fatima Roy): The second. The first was denied in July.

Member (Fatima Roy): They said they called and got the same answer as me.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Fatima Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Fatima Roy): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Fatima Roy): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Fatima Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Cote): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Liam Cote, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Cote): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Cote): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam Cote): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Liam Cote): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Liam Cote): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Liam Cote): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Liam Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Cote): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Liam Cote): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila O'Brien): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): When did you go off work?
Member (Leila O'Brien): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Leila O'Brien): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Leila O'Brien): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Leila O'Brien): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Leila O'Brien): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Leila O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Tyler Kim): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Tyler Kim, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Kim): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Kim): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Tyler Kim): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Tyler Kim): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Tyler Kim): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Tyler Kim): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Tyler Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Tyler Kim): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Tyler Kim): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Tyler Kim): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Tyler Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Noah Kim): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Noah Kim, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Kim): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah Kim): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): How old is he?
Member (Noah Kim): Fourteen.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Noah Kim): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Noah Kim): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Noah Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Noah Kim): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Noah Kim): Great, that helps.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Noah Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Use the 'forgot password' link only once, then wait 30 minutes. I've added a note in case you need to call.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: your account is unlocked, the claim can go in from 6 a.m. Eastern, and there's a note on your file if anything goes wrong.

Member (Lucas Roy): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Lucas Roy, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Lucas Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Lucas Roy): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Lucas Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Lucas Roy): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Lucas Roy): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Lucas Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Lucas Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.

Member (Olivia Patel): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Olivia Patel, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Patel): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Patel): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): How old is he?
Member (Olivia Patel): Fourteen.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Olivia Patel): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Olivia Patel): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Olivia Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Olivia Patel): What's a pre-determination?

Member (Olivia Patel): Great, that helps.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Olivia Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-002142.transcript:
Member (Mei Cote): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Mei Cote, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Cote): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Cote): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Mei Cote): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Mei Cote): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Mei Cote): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Mei Cote): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mei Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Mei Cote): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Mei Cote): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mei Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Member (Liam Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?

Member (Liam Morrison): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Liam Morrison): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
